topic.title: mattiaangeli's knee weights: what data and training code are behind them?

comments.content:
Hi Karan, thanks for asking, and for taking the time to check these! You’re right that the dataset descriptions should be clearer.

For the six releases you listed, the knee-task training used only the competition’s RSNA images and reports—no additional OAI, fastMRI, SKM-TEA, MRNet, KneeMRI or private knee data. This is separate from backbone pretraining: I used public pretrained backbones, including RadImageNet for the explicitly named RadImageNet arm.

The general training approach is similar to this public training notebook, with different architectures, heads and sampling. Most experiments used four public target sets; the recipes differ across releases. There isn’t a hidden dataset or one special trick—mostly several tens experiments, around 60 variants by now 🙂

The published inference code also shows the corresponding architectures, although that is not the same as a complete end-to-end reproduction package for every release.

For M448, its backbone is convnext_small.dinov3_lvd1689m, so the upstream DINOv3 licence applies. “Other” without an explanation is insufficient documentation; it should explicitly identify those terms rather than imply CC0.
Thanks a lot, @mattiaangeli ! That's very clear and helpful: competition data only, public pretrained backbones, and the DINOv3 licence for M448.
